summary: Check whether a binary tree is a mirror of itself.
mainInsight: A tree is symmetric iff its left and right subtrees are mirror images: roots equal, left.left mirrors right.right and left.right mirrors right.left.

approaches.name: Recursive mirror check
approaches.summary: isMirror(a, b): values equal and the crossed children mirror.

approaches.name: Iterative BFS with a queue of pairs

promptVariants: Which children are compared in a mirror check?
How do you test symmetry recursively?
options: Outer pair (left.left, right.right) and inner pair (left.right, right.left)
Left with left and right with right
cards.answer: Outer pair (left.left, right.right) and inner pair (left.right, right.left)
cards.explanation: A mirror crosses the children: the outer nodes face each other and the inner nodes face each other.

promptVariants: How does Symmetric Tree differ from Same Tree?
What changes in the recursive call?
cards.answer: It is Same Tree applied to the left subtree and the mirrored right subtree: instead of pairing left with left, the children are crossed (left of one with right of the other). The base cases and value checks are the same.

promptVariants: Space complexity of the recursion (h = height): ___
Complete the statement: Space complexity of the recursion (h = height): ___
cards.explanation: Call stack depth equals the tree height.

promptVariants: Why does isMirror return False when exactly one of p and q is None?
What does the final line combine?
cards.answer: A mirror image must have a node exactly where the other side has one: one present and one absent breaks symmetry. The last line requires equal values and both crossed child pairs to be mirrors, short-circuiting on the first failure.
cards.explanation: The `not p and not q` base case is the success case.

options: No: both 2s have only a right child (3 and 3), which are not mirrored
cards.answer: No: both 2s have only a right child (3 and 3), which are not mirrored
cards.explanation: Mirrors need the left 2's right child to match the right 2's left child, but the right 2 has none.
